# Research: Database Schema Brush-Up & Auto-Generated Schema Diagram

All product-level unknowns (schema names/grouping, `arxiv_keyword` handling, `data_migrations` disposition, enum requirement, `backend/config.py` scope) were already resolved during `/speckit-clarify` and are recorded in [spec.md](./spec.md)'s Clarifications section. This document covers the remaining **implementation-level** unknowns discovered while investigating the codebase for planning.

## 1. Do we need explicit `GRANT` statements for the moved tables? (FR-006)

- **Decision**: No explicit `GRANT`/`REVOKE` statements are needed for the 5 new schemas (unlike `auth`, which does `REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA auth FROM PUBLIC`).
- **Rationale**: Grepped the entire repo for `CREATE ROLE`, `CREATE USER`, and `GRANT` — the only hit is `auth`'s own `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC` in migration 01. There is no `app_user` (or any other) role ever created via Alembic; both `src/` and `backend/` connect through a single `DATABASE_URL`. Whatever role that connection string authenticates as is the same role that runs `CREATE SCHEMA`/`ALTER TABLE` in every migration, including this one — so it owns every object it creates or moves, and ownership privileges are unaffected by `SET SCHEMA`. The `auth` schema's `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` is defense-in-depth against PostgreSQL's implicit `PUBLIC` grant (relevant for credentials), not evidence of a separate restricted application role.
- **Alternatives considered**: Adding `GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA <x> TO app_user` per new schema, matching a naive reading of the `auth` migration's comment ("scraper's app_user cannot read auth schema"). Rejected — there is no `app_user` role to grant to; the comment describes an aspirational/external role (possibly provisioned manually on Railway, outside version control) that this repo has no evidence of using today for the *primary* connection. Adding a no-op or erroring `GRANT` would be dead code. If such a role does exist in production outside Alembic's visibility, it's a pre-existing gap unrelated to this feature (same exposure already exists for every `public` table today) — noted as a follow-up, not blocking this migration. `vectors` schema (migration 21) precedent confirms this: it adds zero `GRANT`/`REVOKE` statements, only `auth` does.

## 2. Migration shape: one file or several?

- **Decision**: One Alembic revision, `24_reorganize_public_schema_into_ddd_schemas.py`, containing all 5 `CREATE SCHEMA` statements and all 24 `ALTER TABLE ... SET SCHEMA` moves. `downgrade()` reverses every move back to `public` and drops the 5 schemas.
- **Rationale**: This is one atomic logical change (FR-001/FR-002 require it to be fully reversible as a unit); splitting across multiple migrations would only add intermediate states with no independent value and more surface for a partial-apply failure during CI's auto-migrate-on-push. Matches the `auth` (migration 01) and `vectors` (migration 21) precedent of one migration per schema-introduction event.
- **Alternatives considered**: One migration per new schema (5 migrations) — rejected as unnecessary churn for changes that must land together to keep the app working (a partially-migrated state, e.g. `core` created but `intelligence` still in `public`, breaks nothing on its own, but there's no reason to allow that intermediate state given FR-003 already guarantees no data/behavior change either way).

## 3. `ForeignKey(...)` string updates — scope and a cross-boundary edge case

- **Decision**: Every `ForeignKey('<table>.id')` string in `models/*.py` targeting a table that moves MUST become schema-qualified (`ForeignKey('core.articles.id')`), as a **plain literal string** — not routed through the `DbSchema` enum. `__tablename__` values themselves are unaffected (table names don't change, only their schema).
- **Rationale**: `__table_args__['schema']` is the one place FR-011 asks to centralize (it's the single "which schema is THIS table in" declaration, repeated identically across many models in the same group — highest DRY value, highest typo blast radius). `ForeignKey` targets reference a *different* table's `schema.table.column`, already caught immediately by SQLAlchemy's `configure_mappers()`/metadata resolution if wrong (raises at import time, not silently wrong) — lower value in adding enum indirection there, and keeping them plain strings keeps the new diagram-generator's AST parsing simpler (one shape to parse for FK targets, not two).
- **Edge case found**: `models/article_chunk.py` (schema `vectors`, **not** one of the 5 schemas this feature touches — out of scope for the move itself) has `article_id = Column(..., ForeignKey("articles.id", ...))` pointing at the table that *is* moving (`public.articles` → `core.articles`). This FK string MUST still be updated to `"core.articles.id"` even though `ArticleChunk` itself isn't moving, or the reference breaks. Full list of `ForeignKey` strings requiring updates (grepped from `models/*.py`, 2026-07-19): `analyses_translation.py`, `analysis.py`, `article.py` (→ `core.topics.id`), `article_chunk.py` (→ `core.articles.id`, cross-boundary case above), `article_metric_value.py`, `article_metrics.py`, `article_translation.py`, `failed_task.py` (two FKs), `metric_provider.py`, `scraper_keyword.py`, `tag.py` (three FKs, including the `article_tags` association `Table`), `tag_group.py`, `tag_group_translation.py`, `tag_normalization_suggestion.py` (three FKs), `tag_translation.py`, `user_subscription.py` (four FKs across 3 model classes — `auth.users.id` ones are already schema-qualified and untouched, only the `topics.id`/`articles.id` ones change).
- **Alternatives considered**: Routing FK targets through `DbSchema` too (e.g. `ForeignKey(f"{DbSchema.CORE.value}.articles.id")`) for maximum DRY — rejected as over-engineering relative to what FR-011 actually asked for, and it would force the AST-based diagram generator to also parse f-strings (`ast.JoinedStr`) for FK edges, not just for `__table_args__`, with no corresponding safety benefit (SQLAlchemy already catches bad FK targets at startup).

## 4. `__table_args__` shape — dict vs. tuple

- **Decision**: The diagram generator's AST parser MUST handle both shapes seen in this codebase: a plain dict (`models/auth.py`: `__table_args__ = {'schema': 'auth'}`) and a tuple ending in a dict (`models/article_chunk.py`: `__table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint(...), {"schema": "vectors"})`). After this feature, every touched model's schema key holds an `ast.Attribute` chain (`DbSchema.CORE.value`), not a literal string — the parser resolves that by also statically parsing `models/db_schema.py`'s own `MEMBER = "value"` assignments and matching `DbSchema.<MEMBER>` by name, rather than assuming `__table_args__['schema']` is always a string literal.
- **Rationale**: Both shapes already exist in the codebase today (confirmed by reading `models/auth.py` and `models/article_chunk.py`); the parser must not assume one. `auth.py` and `article_chunk.py` themselves are untouched by this feature (their schemas don't move) and will keep their current literal-string form — so the parser needs to support literal strings (for `auth`/`vectors`) *and* enum-attribute resolution (for the 5 new schemas) simultaneously, forever, not just as a migration-period fallback.

## 5. Diagram generation approach: AST-parse vs. runtime import

- **Decision**: Static AST parsing of `models/*.py` (Python stdlib `ast` module), not `import models` + reading `Base.metadata.tables` at runtime.
- **Rationale**: The target workflow step (`speckit-github-pages.yml`) currently only runs `pip install pylint` before the existing `pyreverse`-based UML step — it does **not** run `uv sync` or otherwise install the project's actual runtime dependencies (SQLAlchemy, pydantic, pgvector, etc.). Actually importing `models/` would require installing that whole dependency tree in the docs-build job, a meaningfully heavier and slower CI step than what exists today. Static parsing avoids that entirely and mirrors the existing `pyreverse` step's own static-analysis philosophy (never imports `src/`), keeping the docs pipeline's dependency footprint unchanged. This directly reflects the user's original framing of the request ("依照 AST 的方式").
- **Alternatives considered**: Runtime introspection via `Base.metadata.tables` (perfectly accurate, but requires installing SQLAlchemy + all model-level imports like `pgvector.sqlalchemy.Vector`, `shared.selector_config`, etc. in a job that otherwise stays dependency-light) — rejected for the CI cost reason above, not because it's technically inferior (it is in fact more accurate/robust than hand-parsing `ast.Call` nodes for `Column(...)`/`ForeignKey(...)`, which is a real, accepted tradeoff of the AST approach and should be covered by the generator's own unit tests per the Constitution Check's Test Discipline obligation).

## 6. Diagram rendering format & page integration

- **Decision**: Reuse the already-provisioned Graphviz `dot` toolchain (the workflow already has an "Install Graphviz" step for the UML diagram) to render a static `.svg` from the AST-derived table/column/FK/schema data, embedded in a new `site/guide/architecture/db-schema.md` page. New sidebar/nav entry added alongside the existing "Pipeline"/"Frontend Dependencies" entries in `site/.vitepress/config.js`.
- **Rationale**: Spec's Assumptions already settled this is a **static**, non-interactive page (not a live query tool) — so the existing UML page's much heavier interactive Vue-viewer machinery (`viewer.html`, `uml-data.json` consumed client-side) isn't needed; a plain rendered SVG is sufficient and far simpler to build/maintain. Reusing Graphviz (already installed, already the rendering engine for the sibling UML diagram) keeps visual consistency between the two auto-generated architecture pages without introducing a new rendering dependency (e.g. Mermaid) into the toolchain.
- **Alternatives considered**: Mermaid `erDiagram` syntax (natively supported by VitePress, no Graphviz needed, fully markdown-native/diffable) — a reasonable simpler alternative, deferred to the implementation phase as a fallback if the AST-to-dot generation proves awkward for ER-style layout; noted here so `/speckit-tasks` can pick either without re-researching, but Graphviz is the default given tooling reuse.

## 7. `backend/config.py` — scope and shape

- **Decision**: `backend/config.py` (a single module, matching constitution IX's literal file name — **not** `backend/config/settings.py`, which was left open in spec.md's Assumptions but is now pinned by the already-ratified constitution convention), following `src/config/settings.py`'s existing style: module-level constants, `os.environ.get(...)` reads only, no DB imports, no side effects at import time.
- **Rationale**: Constitution principle IX already mandates this exact file name/location/shape for every FastAPI microservice including `backend/`; this feature is closing a pre-existing compliance gap, not choosing a novel structure. Confirmed via `grep` that `backend/` currently has no `config.py` and reads `os.environ`/`os.getenv` in 23 files (`backend/database.py`, `backend/main.py`, `backend/middleware/logging.py`, `backend/auth/guards.py`, several `backend/services/*.py` and `backend/routers/*.py`, plus test files). Spot-checked that the known env vars (`NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `FRONTEND_ORIGIN`, `VIEW_COUNT_FLUSH_INTERVAL`) already appear in the repo-root `.env.example` — a full cross-check of all ~23 files' vars against `.env.example` is a task-level activity, not a planning risk.
- **Alternatives considered**: A `backend/config/` package (mirroring `src/config/`) — rejected; `src/config/` is a package because `src/` already has other package-level config concerns, but constitution IX is explicit and singular ("`config.py`") for the 3 named FastAPI microservices, and matching it exactly avoids inventing a second convention.

## 8. CRITICAL (found during implementation): integration-test schema isolation needed `schema_translate_map`, not just a `FIXED_SCHEMAS` exclusion

- **Finding**: `src/tests/integration/conftest.py` and `backend/tests/integration/conftest.py` both isolate per-test-run state by creating a throwaway schema (`test_integration` / `backend_test`), setting `search_path=<throwaway>,public` on the test DB engine, and calling `Base.metadata.create_all(...)`. Before this feature, `FIXED_SCHEMAS = {"auth", "vectors"}` excluded only `auth.users`/`vectors.article_chunks` from per-test creation, on the reasoning that explicit-schema tables can't be routed by `search_path` (which only affects *unqualified* names) so they're left pointing at the real, migration-owned schema instead.
- **First (insufficient) fix attempted**: Simply growing `FIXED_SCHEMAS` to include the 5 new schemas. This does stop `create_all()` from erroring, but has a much bigger consequence than the `auth`/`vectors` precedent suggested: unlike `auth.users`/`vectors.article_chunks` (touched directly by very few tests), the 24 moved tables are the tables nearly every integration test touches. Excluding them from per-test isolation meant **every** ORM query against them (via `Article.__table__`, which SQLAlchemy always compiles as fully-qualified `core.articles` regardless of `search_path`) hit the real, shared database — surfacing as 40 failing backend integration tests when checked against the locally-populated dev DB, and 23 still failing against a completely fresh, empty, freshly-migrated database (several tables — `metric_definitions`, `llm_providers`, `scraper_settings`, `metric_providers`, `tag_group_definitions`, `topics` — carry migration-seeded rows even on a brand-new database, so "isolated and empty" was never optional for tests asserting exact/zero counts).
- **Decision**: Use SQLAlchemy's `Engine.execution_options(schema_translate_map={...})` — the built-in, documented mechanism for exactly this scenario. Mapping `{"core": TEST_SCHEMA, "collection": TEST_SCHEMA, "intelligence": TEST_SCHEMA, "ai_infra": TEST_SCHEMA, "user_prefs": TEST_SCHEMA}` on the per-test-session engine makes SQLAlchemy rewrite every compiled `<schema>.<table>` reference — DDL (`create_all`) and DML (ORM queries, Core `update()`/`delete()`) alike — to `TEST_SCHEMA.<table>` at execution time, collapsing all 5 real schemas into the one isolated per-test schema. `FIXED_SCHEMAS` reverts to just `{"auth", "vectors"}` (its original, pre-feature value) since the 24 tables are no longer excluded — they're translated instead.
- **Follow-up limitation found**: `schema_translate_map` explicitly does **not** apply to raw `text()` SQL (SQLAlchemy docs: takes effect for DDL/DML other than constructs "entirely composed of literal SQL text"). Repository code with raw SQL against moved tables (`tag_repo_impl.py`, `tag_group_definition_repo_impl.py`, `backend/routers/tags.py`, `backend/services/{tag_service,article_service,scraper_settings_service}.py`) was initially hardcoded to the new schema-qualified names (e.g. `UPDATE collection.article_metrics ...`) as part of FR-005 — but a schema-qualified literal is exactly what `schema_translate_map` *can't* rewrite, so those two specific tests (`test_flush_view_counts_moves_redis_counts_into_article_metrics`, `test_merge_deduplicates_tags_with_same_name`) failed even after the `schema_translate_map` fix: the raw SQL wrote to the real schema while the ORM-created test fixture row lived in the translated one.
- **Final decision (supersedes the raw-SQL half of FR-005's original literal reading)**: Keep raw SQL **unqualified**, exactly as it was pre-migration, and instead set the default `search_path` at the **database** level in migration 24's `upgrade()` (`ALTER DATABASE "<db>" SET search_path TO core, collection, intelligence, ai_infra, user_prefs, public`). This means: production raw SQL keeps resolving unqualified names correctly (via the new default search_path) exactly as before the migration; test raw SQL resolves via the test engine's own `search_path=TEST_SCHEMA,public` into the isolated schema, consistently with ORM queries (translated via `schema_translate_map`) — both mechanisms land in the same place. `ForeignKey(...)` strings in `models/*.py` are unaffected by this reversal — those remain schema-qualified (§3 above), since SQLAlchemy compiles them from Table metadata, not raw text, so they were never subject to this limitation. Spec.md's FR-005 explicitly allowed either approach ("updated to the new schema-qualified name (**or rely on `search_path`**)") — this is that second option, chosen after the first was found to conflict with test isolation.
- **Tradeoff accepted**: unqualified names now resolve via a 6-schema `search_path` instead of being self-documenting at each call site; a future table added to two different schemas with the same name would create silent ambiguity (todady none exists — all 24+2 table names are globally unique). Judged acceptable given it exactly preserves pre-existing raw-SQL conventions and avoids a much larger refactor (converting every raw-SQL repository method to SQLAlchemy Core constructs) that this feature's scope doesn't call for.
- **Verification**: confirmed against a disposable, freshly-`alembic upgrade head`-ed throwaway Postgres container (not the locally-populated dev DB) that all `src/` (80) and `backend/` (224) integration tests pass, in addition to both suites passing against the real local dev database (304 total) and both full unit suites (1033 total, `src/` 701 + `backend/` 332) — 1337 tests green end to end.
